title: It takes time
author: Leone239
selftext:
Wsp guys, I just want to thank this sub first because the first time I ever seen what algo trading is, was in this sub when i joined in january this year, after 10 months of 1000 different algos created, backtested and modified I trusted one and made 4.6k this month since i switched from prop firms to personal account.

Im not selling anything but just wanted to show u guys its possible, willing to answer any questions but im not a pro still, also attached the backtest of this year. And before u say its only a year of backtesting the strategy its based around works always because its similar to scalping, also backtested last 3 years and it works

comments.author: Signal_Pace_7968
comments.body:
Congrats, that’s a good month. Two questions since you offered:

Did you test it on a period you didn’t look at while building it? With 1000 versions tried, a few will look good on the same data just by chance, so a test on unseen data is what tells them apart.

And how close is the live month to what the backtest says for the same weeks? For something close to scalping, fills and fees are usually where the gap shows up first.

replies.author: Leone239
replies.body: I forward tested only the top 100 that performed on the backtest, the backtest is around 99% correct because i used a backtest software that included the average spread at the times EA took the trades, also slippage was added and the standard fee of 2 lots was included so the real trading may be a little bit better than backtest or a little bit worse but still its pretty accurate

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: Those are the right two questions, and the second one is the easiest to answer: put the live month's trades next to the backtest's trades for the same weeks and compare the average win, the average loss and how many trades each took. If the live average is much smaller, the gap is costs and fills. Thanks for putting it clearly.

comments.author: YojoNick
comments.body:
Going through a thousand different algorithms in 10 months is really impressive. Would you be willing to share more about how you did that? Were the algorithms mechanical? Were they all deep learning-based? Perhaps a mix?  Did you have a similar backtesting methodology for all of them? What was your process for vetting algorithms?   
  
Those are kind of a lot of questions. Feel free to answer one of them or none of them at all. I'm just really intrigued by 1,000 algos in 10 months. That's a wonderful example of fail fast, fail often, fail forward.

replies.author: Leone239
replies.body: wow the last thing u said is so true, to answer your questions im not sure what u mean by mechanical or deep learning-based but for backtesting i always backtested first than if the backtest was promising i forward tested it and based on the results i either kept it or scrapped it and then moved to another one, once i had top 100 performers i analyzed every single one and seen what worked and what didnt, after that i made the one i use today by merging the best of the top 100 algos i picked

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Congrats on the live month, that's the real test. Two numbers on the backtest report caught my eye: a Sharpe of 15.94 is far higher than anything that survives live trading, and almost all entries fall in one hour (around 7 to 8 in the chart), which makes me think the result leans on one very specific window. After 1,000 algos tried, the one you picked is the best of a big pile, so the live months from here are the honest sample, and I'd keep them separate from the backtest. I'd also check how it handles spread and slippage at that hour, since scalpers lose their edge there first. Cymetica's Backtest Labs is one place to see how strategy results get compared against a benchmark.
